放.meaning: On the last night of summer, a girl puts her jar of fireflies on a toy raft with a paper <part>sail</part> and waves a <part>fan</part> to push it across the pond. Halfway over, the lid pops and a hundred lights float up into the dark. She has <kanji>set free</kanji> every one.
放.on: Her little brother, less patient, blasts the raft the rest of the way with the garden <sound>ho</sound>se.
放.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' she laughs, and lets her goldfish go too, with a crumb of <sound>na</sound>an for the trip.

量.meaning: At <part>daybreak</part> on the <part>farm</part>, the hens hold a contest. The farmer piles each hen's eggs on a seesaw against sacks of flour until it balances. It isn't the best egg that wins, only the <kanji>quantity</kanji>.
量.on: The winning hen gets a weekend at a <sound>ryo</sound>kan, an inn with paper doors and a hot bath.
量.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' laughs the farmer, as she measures a <sound>ca</sound>rp that has flopped onto the seesaw too.

石.meaning: A rock tumbles off a cliff ledge and lands in a meadow, square as a box. A child paints a <part>mouth</part> on it, and it starts grumbling about the rain, the cold and the sheep sitting on it. It's still just a <kanji>stone</kanji>, only now a moody one.
石.on: The child paints a pie chart on its back, with one <sound>sec</sound>tor for each thing it hates.
石.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>!' it squeals, as a <sound>shee</sound>p plonks down on its face again.

蔵.meaning: Under a thatch of <part>grass</part>, a door is carved into the <part>cliff</part>, and a <part>servant</part> with a <part>spear</part> guards it day and night. Behind him are sacks of rice, jars of honey and every winter coat in the valley. It's the village's secret <kanji>storehouse</kanji>.
蔵.on: The door is painted with the twelve signs of the <sound>zo</sound>diac, one shelf of stock for each month.
蔵.kun: Every hour a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo pops out above the door, and the servant gives a sleepy '<sound>Rah</sound>!'

庫.meaning: The <part>shed</part> at the end of the garden looks too small for a bike, yet every night another <part>car</part> drives in and none drive out. Open the door and it goes back for miles: rows of cars, pianos, boats. It's a giant <kanji>warehouse</kanji>.
庫.on: The night guard is a <sound>ko</sound>ala, fast asleep in the front seat of the very first car.
庫.kun: Somewhere deep in the dark a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo clock strikes, and the koala jolts awake with a '<sound>Rah</sound>!'

得.meaning: At <part>daybreak</part>, a golfer rides the <part>chairlift</part> to the top of the mountain with one <part>golf club</part> and one ball. She tees off, the ball bounces down the slopes for an hour and drops into the hole. One shot, and a whole cabinet of trophies to <kanji>gain</kanji>.
得.on: All that hour, the clubhouse clock goes tick-<sound>tock</sound>, tick-tock.
得.kun: '<sound>Eh</sound>?' gasps her caddie, as she gets a gold cup, a goat and a year of free lessons.

党.meaning: Your <part>big brother</part> is held in such <part>esteem</part> at school that he starts a club with its own flag, badge and slogan: 'Pizza Every Friday.' By lunch, half the school has signed up. It's a political <kanji>party</kanji>, all about pizza.
党.on: Every member keeps their badge taped to one big <sound>toe</sound>, for secret checks.
党.kun: At meetings they share a <sound>na</sound>an and a grilled <sound>ca</sound>rp, and even his <sound>Ma</sound> has joined: they're all comrades.

軍.meaning: Under a huge green <part>blanket</part> in the field, something rumbles. Lift one corner: a <part>car</part>, then another, then a thousand, all painted in leafy colours, engines ticking. The blanket is hiding a whole <kanji>army</kanji>.
軍.on: Its general is Big <sound>Gun</sound>ther, who sleeps in the first car with his boots on.
軍.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>k!' cries a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo as the war begins, and the cars roll out, pelting the enemy with <sound>sa</sound>rdines.

再.meaning: Every night a kitten knocks <part>one</part> plate off the top of the kitchen <part>cabinet</part>. Every morning Grandad glues it back and puts it up there. Crash, glue, shelf; crash, glue, shelf. Tomorrow it will happen <kanji>again</kanji>.
再.on: To stay calm, Grandad pours himself a glass of <sound>ci</sound>der every single time.
再.kun: The kitten naps on a <sound>fu</sound>ton, eats a <sound>ta</sound>co, then a second <sound>ta</sound>co, and climbs the cabinet once more.

組.meaning: At the knitting club, each member ties one <part>thread</part> to the next, while the chair keeps adding 'and <part>moreover</part>' to the rules: no cats, moreover no biscuits, moreover no dropped stitches. By midnight they're all knotted into one big woolly <kanji>association</kanji>.
組.on: The whole meeting takes place on one long, squashy <sound>so</sound>fa.
組.kun: At midnight a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo pops out of the clock and grabs a thread, so now it's teamed up with them too.

砂.meaning: A sculptor keeps chipping at a <part>stone</part>, aiming for the perfect statue. Every day there's a <part>few</part> bits less of it: a boulder, a brick, a pebble, a crumb. In the end, all that's left of her masterpiece is a pinch of <kanji>sand</kanji>.
砂.on: She sweeps it into an empty <sound>sa</sound>rdine tin and calls it art.
砂.kun: The tin sits on a beach stall between the <sound>su</sound>shi and the <sound>na</sound>an, and nobody notices it at all.

糖.meaning: In a palace of old <part>china</part>, the cooks boil a pot of <part>rice</part> for a hundred days, stirring until it turns to sticky, sparkling white crystals. The emperor licks one spoonful and grins. They have invented <kanji>sugar</kanji>.
糖.on: He eats so much that a sugar lump rolls off the table and lands on his big <sound>toe</sound>.

活.meaning: On the hottest day of the year, a frog lies flat on a lily pad, too limp to croak, until a few <part>water drops</part> land on its <part>tongue</part>. It blinks, and suddenly it's leaping from pad to pad, singing and splashing everyone. Nothing in the pond is as <kanji>lively</kanji>.
活.on: It celebrates by gulping down a crumbed <sound>katsu</sound> cutlet in one go.
活.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>k!' squeals a dragonfly, as the frog everyone thought was done for springs up: it lives!

育.meaning: A woman finds a baby <part>moon</part> no bigger than a plum and keeps it in a jar with a <part>lid</part>. She rocks it in the crook of her <part>elbow</part>, feeds it starlight, and every month it grows rounder. Year after year she will <kanji>bring up</kanji> the moon.
育.on: '<sound>Ee</sound>!' she squeals, shooing away a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo that tries to lay its egg in the jar.
育.kun: It grows up on the <sound>so</sound>fa, watching her throw <sound>da</sound>rts at the stars.

応.meaning: A lonely <part>heart</part> spots a sign on a garden <part>shed</part>: 'Wanted: someone to keep the hens warm.' It fills in the form, draws itself a smile and slides it under the door. It's the first job it has ever dared to <kanji>apply</kanji> for.
応.on: The interview is held under a huge <sound>oa</sound>k, and the hens ask all the questions.
応.kun: A <sound>ko</sound>ala answers the shed door with the result: '<sound>Ta</sound>-da! You're hired!'

界.meaning: A beetle lives <part>jammed in</part> between the squares of one <part>rice field</part>, squeezed so tight it can't see past the next stalk. It thinks the paddy is everything there is. To the beetle, this one field is the whole <kanji>world</kanji>.
界.on: One day a <sound>ki</sound>te string snags it and lifts it high, and it sees a million more fields.

資.meaning: An octopus lines up its treasures in its den: one <part>shellfish</part> shell, then the <part>next</part>, then the next, each a bit shinier, counted every evening with all eight arms. Then it writes them all in a little ledger. These shells are its <kanji>assets</kanji>.
資.on: It guards the den with a rusty knight's <sound>shi</sound>eld it found in a shipwreck.

然.meaning: A <part>dog</part> roasts sausages over <part>hot coals</part> by the light of the <part>moon</part>, listening to the campers' tall tales. Each time someone claims they wrestled a bear, it raises one eyebrow and says, 'Is that <kanji>so</kanji>?'
然.on: Later, while they sleep, the dog rakes the cold ashes into neat lines like a <sound>zen</sound> garden.
然.kun: '<sound>She</sound> wrestled a <sound>ca</sound>rp, however!' adds one camper, but the dog only yawns.

位.meaning: In the castle hall, every guest gets a <part>coat hook</part> and a spot to <part>stand</part> below it, and the higher the hook, the closer to the king you stand. The duke's hook is up by the ceiling; the cook's is by the floor. Just look up and you know everyone's <kanji>rank</kanji>.
位.on: The lowest hook of all holds a dripping <sound>ee</sound>l in a tiny coat.
位.kun: A <sound>cu</sound>ckoo on the king's hook nibbles <sound>rye</sound> bread: the higher the hook, the better the bread.

棒.meaning: A beaver chews a whole <part>tree</part> down to one long, straight branch and holds it up as an <part>offer</part> to the beaver she fancies. He inspects it, taps it on a rock and nods. It's the finest <kanji>rod</kanji> in the river.
棒.on: Together they use it to lever a huge <sound>bou</sound>lder into place on their new dam.

泥.meaning: A very proper <part>nun</part> walks to church in her best white robe, until the first <part>water drops</part> of a storm fall. She looks left, looks right, hitches up her skirt and leaps into the deepest puddle with a whoop. She's splattered from head to toe in <kanji>mud</kanji>.
泥.on: 'Best <sound>day</sound> ever!' she laughs, wringing out her veil.
泥.kun: A <sound>do</sound>lphin and a <sound>ro</sound>dent jump into the puddle right after her.

覚.meaning: Every night a girl hides under her <part>blanket</part> with a <part>camera</part>, flicking through photos of the times tables. When a sum finally sticks, <part>fireworks</part> burst over her head. By morning she can shut her eyes and see every page: she's managed to <kanji>memorize</kanji> them all.
覚.on: To test her, her brother flashes a picture of a crow's <sound>carc</sound>ass for one second, and she names every bone.
覚.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' she gasps, and suddenly remembers where she hid her <sound>bo</sound>nsai.

続.meaning: A market trader tries to <part>sell</part> one <part>thread</part> to a knitter. He pulls and pulls, and it keeps coming out of his sleeve, across the square and down to the river. The knitter keeps knitting. Neither can stop, so the sale has to <kanji>continue</kanji>.
続.on: By midnight, <sound>Zo</sound>e from the flower stall and her pet <sound>cu</sound>ckoo are knitting along too.
続.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' sneezes the trader, and the thread keeps on spooling, round a <sound>zu</sound>cchini, a cart and a cow.

違.meaning: Two toy <part>pagoda</part> towers that look like twins race side by side down a <part>ramp</part>. At the bottom they still look the same, until you count the roofs: one has five, the other six. Can you spot the <kanji>difference</kanji>?
違.on: The prize for spotting it is a wriggling <sound>ee</sound>l in a jar.
違.kun: A <sound>chee</sound>tah sniffs them both: one smells of <sound>ga</sound>rlic, the other doesn't.

勝.meaning: At the strongman contest, every <part>bodybuilder</part> lifts a car or a cow. The last one walks out at midnight, bends his knees and hoists the <part>moon</part> above his head. The crowd goes silent, then wild. Nobody else stood a chance: total <kanji>victory</kanji>.
勝.on: His moon lift becomes the star of the big <sound>show</sound> on stage the next night.
勝.kun: His trophy is a golden <sound>ca</sound>rp, and he wins one more round by holding it up with one finger.

退.meaning: A clunky <part>robot</part> marches up the <part>ramp</part> to conquer the kitchen, until the cat hisses at it. It freezes, beeps twice, then rolls backwards down the ramp as fast as its wheels will spin. Brave robot, wise <kanji>retreat</kanji>.
退.on: As it flees, its little bow <sound>tie</sound> spins round like a propeller.
退.kun: It backs off behind a <sound>shee</sound>p, a <sound>ree</sound>f of sofa cushions and a girl called <sound>Zo</sound>e.

旦.meaning: A lazy rooster dozes on <part>one</part> fence rail, eyes shut. The <part>sun</part> climbs up and sits on the rail right above him, nudging his back. 'Five more minutes,' he mutters, but the sky is already pink. He's slept through <kanji>daybreak</kanji> again.
旦.on: He crows anyway, from deep inside a dark <sound>tun</sound>nel, where it still feels like night.
旦.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' In the new light he spots the lost barn <sound>key</sound> glinting in the grass: plain as day.

那.meaning: A knight rides into town with a <part>sword</part> in one hand and a <part>pennant</part> in the other, shouting a challenge nobody understands. <part>Two</part> villagers squint at the flag, then at each other, and shrug: '<kanji>What?</kanji>'
那.on: It turns out all he wants is to swap his sword for one warm <sound>na</sound>an.
那.kun: 'A <sound>na</sound>an? Down on one <sound>knee</sound>? For bread?' the villagers ask, as he kneels to beg.

接.meaning: On a sinking ship, a <part>woman</part> hugs the <part>anchor</part> and rides it down to the sea floor, where she plants her feet to <part>stand</part>. She reaches out one finger to a sleeping whale's nose. Just one tiny <kanji>touch</kanji>, and the whale opens an eye.
接.on: The whale yawns, and out swims a soggy red <sound>set</sound>ter, paddling for the surface.
接.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' sneezes the whale, and a stream of bubbles joins it to the boat above.

参.meaning: A <part>large</part> walrus with droopy <part>whiskers</part> knocks on your door with one <part>elbow</part>, because his flippers are full of fish. He's come all the way from the ice for tea. It's his yearly <kanji>visit</kanji>.
参.on: He brings you an ice cream <sound>sun</sound>dae, with a sardine on top.
参.kun: '<sound>My</sound>, what a big guest!' says Grandma, as he squeezes in through the door.
